study.title: Integration patterns of functional brain networks can predict the response to abdominal acupuncture in patients with major depressive disorder
study.study_design: Blinded, randomized, controlled study; two parallel arms, both receiving oral fluoxetine plus either real or sham abdominal acupuncture; resting-state fMRI acquired at pre- and post-treatment
study.randomization: Patients were randomly assigned to undergo real abdominal acupuncture or sham abdominal acupuncture
study.blinding: Participants wore a blindfold and mask during treatment; not explicitly stated whether outcome assessors or investigators were blinded
study.population: Female patients with major depressive disorder (MDD), recruited through gynecology outpatient clinic of Guangdong Provincial Hospital of Chinese Medicine
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) women meeting the ICD-10 criteria for depressive disorder; (2) self-rating depressive disorder scale (SDS) score ≥ 53 points or Montgomery–Åsberg depression rating scale (MADRS) score ≥ 14 points; (3) age 30–60 years and signing the informed consent form to join the clinical trial; (4) right-handed, with primary school education or above; and (5) normal cognitive function and no aphasia or mental retardation.
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) refusal to provide informed consent to participate in the trial; (2) pregnant or breastfeeding women; (3) having metal implants in the body; (4) using antipsychotic drugs or antidepressants within 1 month before participation in the study; (5) addiction to alcohol or use of illegal drugs; (6) severe liver or kidney damage, impaired neurological function, rheumatism, heart disease, diabetes, malignant tumors, or any other major systemic diseases that may affect the results; (7) severe mental illness (schizophrenia, mania, paranoid psychosis, suicidal intention, depressive disorder) or dementia; and (8) any physical diseases that may affect the study results. (such as cerebral infarction, cerebral hemorrhage, Parkinson's disease, brain tumor, or other major systemic diseases).

interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: Abdominal acupoints were selected based on traditional Chinese medicine theory. CV8 (umbilicus) was selected as the main acupoint because it plays a critical role in promoting and regulating airflow. Other acupoints selected because they are near important meridians and easily communicate with the five Zang and six Fu organs through channels such as meridians, blood vessels, thoracic meridians, and belt meridians. This acupuncture prescription can coordinate qi stagnation in the five Zang organs, replenish qi and blood, and thereby relieve depressive disorder.

extraction_notes.note: No formal deqi questionnaire or measurement instrument was used. Sensation was described only qualitatively as 'mild sensation' for real acupuncture. No quantitative sensory or deqi data were reported.
Expectancy, credibility, and blinding success were not assessed or reported. Neither the methods nor results section mentions any credibility or expectancy scale.
The paper does not report whether outcome assessors or investigators were blinded. Only participant blinding (via blindfold/mask during treatment) is mentioned.

The SDS post-minus-pre values in Table 1 appear to show one entry as '−21.00 (−12.5)' for real acupuncture and '−12.50 (8.65)' for sham. The format is ambiguous — it may represent median (IQR) or mean (SD) with non-normal distribution, consistent with the methods statement about non-normally distributed variables being expressed as median and interquartile range. The extraction preserves the exact table values.

The paper abbreviates the CCN alternately as 'CCN' and 'CNN' in different sections. The full name is 'cognitive control network.' This appears to be a typographical inconsistency in the original paper. Both terms are preserved as encountered.

The abstract states 'SN–DMN, SN–AN, and intra-DMN' as predictive of treatment efficacy, but the results section and Tables 2 and 3 indicate that the predictive masks used are from the AN (sgACC seed) and DMN (PCC seed) analyses. The Discussion section states 'baseline FC values of SN–DMN, SN–AN, and intra-DMN were found to be predictive.' This appears inconsistent with Table 3 which shows AN and DMN masks were used for SVR prediction. The extraction preserves actual numerical results from the results section and Table 3.

Table 2 header states threshold as 'voxel-wise p < 0.005, uncorrected' but the methods section states the primary threshold is 'voxel-wise p < 0.001 uncorrected.' The footnote clarifies that the asterisk (*) rows used small volume correction with 'voxel-wise p < 0.005 uncorrected.' Both thresholds were applied and are noted.

The F value column in Table 2 shows values such as 19.13, 21.31, 15.29, etc. These are listed alongside peak z values. It is unclear whether these F values correspond to the interaction term from the repeated-measures ANOVA at the peak voxel or represent a different statistic. Both z values and F values from Table 2 are extracted; only z values are labelled as peak statistics per table header.

The con_007 partial correlation (DLPFC–mPFC vs. MADRS) is reported in the results text as correlated with 'MADRS score improvement' but the figure caption (Fig. 4C) labels the x-axis as 'The SDS score improvement after treatment (post-pre).' This is internally inconsistent. The text was used as primary source; the figure caption discrepancy is noted here.

The paper states two groups were merged for MVPA analysis: 'we merged 2 groups of patients in the MVPA analysis.' The n_analyzed for con_008 and con_009 is therefore 36 (all completers), not 18 per group.
No healthy control group was included. The study only includes MDD patients in two treatment arms, so no between-patient and healthy-control neuroimaging comparisons are possible.
No data on prior acupuncture experience of participants was reported.

The exact number of acupuncture sessions per participant is not directly stated as a total count. The schedule was: 'once a day for the first 3 days and then once every 3 days for the rest of the 8-week trial.' Total session count can be computed but is not directly stated in the paper.

The paper refers to the DMN seed as 'bilateral posterior cingulate cortex (DMN: PCC, ±11, −58, 17)' but results from Table 2 and Fig. 3 refer only to the 'left PCC.' The seed appears bilateral per methods but only left-hemisphere results survived the threshold. The contrast labels reflect this.
The Conclusions section refers to 'between the AN and DMA' which appears to be a typographical error for 'between the AN and DMN.' The extraction uses the correct intended term DMN.
